Fixed a JSON validity issue in zh-CN.json: the edit_file tool transcribed Chinese typographic quotation marks U+201C/U+201D as ASCII double-quotes (U+0022), breaking JSON string delimiters. Replaced the conflicting characters with CJK corner brackets 「」 which are unambiguous in JSON.

zh-CN translations follow all Asian locale rules: full-width punctuation (。，：), aki spacing between English/numerics and Chinese chars (e.g., '已移除 {0} 个 MOD'), and 「」 corner brackets for UI element references.
ja-JP translations follow all Asian locale rules: full-width punctuation, aki spacing (e.g., '{0} 個の MOD が削除されました'), and 「」 Japanese quotation marks.
All 466 tests pass including AllLocaleFiles_HaveAllKeys_FromBaseLocale, AllLocaleFiles_AreValidJson, and AllLocaleFiles_PreserveFormatPlaceholders.

comments.note: The edit_file tool silently transcribes Unicode typographic quotation marks (U+201C LEFT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK, U+201D RIGHT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK) as ASCII 34 (U+0022 QUOTATION MARK). In JSON string values, this breaks the JSON because the parser interprets the characters as string terminators. Any future translations that use typographic double-quotes ('smart quotes') must use 「」 corner brackets or \" escape sequences instead. This should be noted in the localization guide as a tooling constraint.

The 7 locale files use flat key ordering within the DiffDialog section. CountFormat and CountSingular pairs (e.g., GuidanceRemovalCountFormat / GuidanceRemovalCountSingular) are adjacent, but there is no structural grouping to enforce this. A future refactor could add comments (not valid in JSON) or adopt a JSONC/YAML format with comment support to make the pairing relationships self-documenting.

zh-CN uses 「」 corner brackets for UI element names in body text (GuidanceRemovalBody, GuidanceInsertionBody) while other body text strings in the same locale use no quotation marks. This is consistent with the localization guide's intent but uses 「」 rather than the guide's specified " " marks due to the tooling constraint described above. The approach is internally consistent within the zh-CN file.

[documentation-forward] localization.md Section 3 (Quotation Marks) specifies Chinese quotes " " (U+201C/U+201D) for zh-CN UI element references (e.g. '"Profiles" 文件夹'). However, these codepoints cannot be safely stored in JSON via the edit_file toolchain — they are silently transcribed as ASCII 34 (plain double-quote), breaking JSON parsing. The actual implementation correctly uses 「」 (U+300C/U+300D) as the JSON-safe alternative. The localization.md guide must be updated to: (1) document the tooling constraint, (2) specify 「」 as the approved alternative for zh-CN when typographic quotes are required, and (3) align the anti-pattern list to reflect this. Without this update, future zh-CN translators will follow the guide and introduce JSON-breaking strings.

The CountFormat/CountSingular pairing convention is well-executed across all 7 locales — all CountFormat keys preserve {0} and CountSingular keys correctly hardcode '1'. The it-IT locale makes a good stylistic choice using the Italian combined form 'mod rimosso/i' and 'mod inserito/i' for the count strings, which is idiomatic and avoids the parenthesised '(s)' construction used in other Western locales. This is a minor translation style choice, not a defect.
